tagline.text: Southeast Asia's first large multipurpose dam, straddling the Isabela–Ifugao border

location.label: Location
location.text: Ramon, Isabela (on the Alfonso Lista, Ifugao boundary, Namillangan village)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May (check release announcements in the rainy and typhoon season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300–1,500 (round trip in one day from Cauayan or Santiago; local transport and meals, estimated)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Cauayan Airport (CYZ) or Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Manila (MNL), then overland

children.text: Magat Dam is a 114 m high rock-fill dam completed in 1982, spanning Ramon in Isabela and Alfonso Lista in Ifugao. It serves irrigation, flood control and hydropower, and is a quiet place for a walk with views of the reservoir and the Ifugao mountains.

Magat Dam is a large rock-fill dam on the Magat River in northern Luzon. The Magat River is the largest tributary of the Cagayan River; it rises in Nueva Vizcaya and joins the Cagayan River in Isabela. According to Wikipedia, the dam is in Namillangan village on the boundary between Ramon, Isabela and Alfonso Lista, Ifugao, about
350 km
north of Manila. One blog gives about
from Manila (a 7.5-hour drive), about
from Cauayan City and about
from Ilagan City.
The
National Irrigation Administration dam specifications
give a height of
and a crest length of

. At full supply, the water surface is 193 meters above sea level and covers about 45 square kilometers. The dam supplies irrigation water and supports hydropower as part of the Magat River Multipurpose Project.

The history begins with Presidential Decree No. 693, signed by Ferdinand Marcos on May 7, 1975, which authorized the project. Wikipedia gives the start of construction as 1975 in one place and 1978 in another, so sources disagree. The dam was inaugurated on October 27, 1982 and began operating in 1983. The World Bank lent US$150 million for foreign exchange costs, and the dam is described as Southeast Asia's first large multipurpose dam. It was designed to last 50 years, but siltation, slash-and-burn farming, illegal logging and the 1990 Luzon earthquake degraded the watershed, and in January 2006 the president at the time ordered a rehabilitation plan.

Management is split between two parties. The National Irrigation Administration (NIA) owns and operates the dam, reservoir and intake gates, while the power plant was privatized under the Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001 and has been operated by SN Aboitiz Power–Magat (SNAP-Magat) since April 2007. The plant has four 90 MW Francis turbines for an installed capacity of 360 MW and is a peaking plant that mainly runs when demand is high. A refurbishment that began in 2009 was completed in June 2014, and a 24 MW battery storage system was added in 2024. One blog says a floating solar project was inaugurated in June 2019. The powerhouse is designed to take two more units, which would raise capacity to 540 MW. Wikipedia gives the project cost as US$3.4 billion in 1975 value. A US$9 million loan from Bahrain reportedly paid for diversion tunnel equipment, a soil laboratory and model testing.

blocks.title: Walkway on the dam and lake views

children.text: At Magat Dam on the Ramon side, look over the reservoir and Ifugao mountains from public areas. Follow entrance signs for which parts of the dam crest are open to pedestrians and where vehicle access is restricted.

The large spillway, about 500 m long and about 164 m wide, has seven radial gates and two orifice gates. They are normally closed, but this is the structure that passes large flows during typhoons, so you can get a sense of its scale.

The plant has four 90 MW generators. One blog shows it mostly in photos, and no confirmed information is available on whether visitors can tour the inside. If you want a tour, ask the operator in advance.
From the dam you can see the boundary marker for Alfonso Lista, Ifugao, and the bridge over the river. Standing on the border between two provinces is what makes this place unusual.
View the reservoir from the public area on the Ramon side. The
National Irrigation Administration reservoir rules
specify fishing permits and a protected zone. Ask the reservoir office about tourist boat availability, permits and permitted areas before arranging fishing or a boat ride.
A floating solar installation of about 2,500 m² is reportedly on the reservoir. It is worth a look if you are interested in renewable energy.
Camp Vizcarra Ecology Park in Ramon is close to the dam. One blog listed a low admission fee, but check the current rate on site.
Take a vehicle from Cauayan or Santiago toward Ramon and get off at the Magat Dam junction.
Take a tricycle to the dam and ask at the gate for guidance. Ask the local staff about visiting rules.
Walk the crest, look at the lake and mountains, and rest in the sheds.
Photograph the boat station, spillway and boundary marker.
Enjoy the view at dusk and return to Ramon town before dark.
The 2017 reviewer did not actually see the sunset but guessed it would be stunning. Go on a clear day.
Have breakfast in Cauayan and head to Ramon. It is about 1 hour by car from Cauayan to the dam.
Have lunch in Ramon town and look around Camp Vizcarra Ecology Park.
Go to Magat Dam for a walk and the views.
Return to Cauayan or Santiago.

items.title: From Santiago or Cauayan to Ramon

children.text: A 2017 review advises taking a jeepney or van from Santiago toward Ramon and getting off at the junction to Magat Dam.
From the junction you go to the dam by tricycle. The same review gave the fare as
per passenger one way, or
one way to hire the whole tricycle. This is old information, so confirm the current fare with the driver.
The dam and reservoir are reached by an all-weather road connecting to the San Mateo–Santiago Road at Oscariz.
Whether Cauayan Airport (CYZ) is served from Manila must be checked directly with the airlines. After arriving, the dam is about
from Cauayan, roughly
1 hour
by car.

Because the visit involves walking on a dam with little shade at midday, the cooler November–February period is the most comfortable. March–May is hot, so it is better to go in the late afternoon and time your visit for sunset.

Check for water releases in typhoon season. When Typhoon Vamco (locally Ulysses) crossed the country in November 2020, Magat Dam opened all its gates and released a large volume of water into the Cagayan River, causing heavy flooding in Isabela and Cagayan downstream. In the rainy season, check the release announcements from PAGASA and NIA, and do not go on days of heavy rain.

Santiago City is convenient for onward transport to Ramon. A day trip from Cauayan is also possible if you arrange return transport from Ramon and the dam junction. Ask the municipality separately about camping or lodging at Camp Vizcarra.
Bring water and food for the dam. The
Emm’s Fried Chicken Santiago menu
lists oven-roasted chicken with rice at
. If your route bypasses Santiago, arrange a meal in Ramon town.
Going in the late afternoon means fewer people and a chance to see the sunset, but leave before your return transport stops running.
You will be walking on a dam with almost no shade, so bring a hat, water and sunscreen.
The
Philippine Information Agency’s 2026 report
describes Ramon’s tourism hub as a proposal. Stay in designated visitor areas and follow site staff instructions around the power plant and gates.
Call the
National Irrigation Administration’s Magat Dam and Reservoir Division
at +63 999 221 7686 to check which areas are open and when.
When you hire a tricycle from Ramon to the dam, agree on the return ride at the same time.
When a typhoon is approaching, first check the release announcements and flood forecasts.

Water releases can change the water level downstream suddenly, so stay away from the river's edge and follow announcements and staff instructions after rain. The inquiry email is isabelatourismoffice@gmail.com.
When the dam releases large volumes in a typhoon, areas downstream in Isabela and Cagayan are heavily flooded. Always check the release announcements before a rainy-season visit.
During Typhoon Ulysses in November 2020, the dam opened its seven gates to 24 m and released water, flooding the lower Cagayan River. The NIA later said it would review its release protocols.
Check the public area and Camp Vizcarra separately for hours and fees. Water releases and maintenance can change access.
Stay within areas designated by the operator along the reservoir and river. Follow posted rules on swimming and access to the water.
One blog said tourist fishing and boating had been halted, so if you plan to take a boat, first check whether it is operating.
Return transport may be limited, so go back to town before dark.
An ecology park in Ramon, close to the dam. Good for a walk and a rest.

blocks.title: Fuyot Springs National Park and Ilagan Sanctuary

children.text: Protected areas in Ilagan City, Isabela, known for caves and a tree-top adventure. About an hour and a half from the dam by car.
One of the main cities of Isabela, about 40 km from the dam; a good place to find lodging and restaurants.
World Heritage rice terraces toward Ifugao to the west. They can be added to an itinerary linking Isabela and Ifugao.
